project.objective: Who was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont?

questions.question: Who was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont?
questions.rationale: This is the project's sole research objective — identifying the father of William A. Bagley. Vermont vital records, census records, and probate records from the early-to-mid 19th century offer plausible avenues for establishing a father-son relationship for a man born about 1815 and resident in Topsham, Orange County. The death date (31 May 1884) is specific and anchors the subject confidently; the birth year is approximate but consistent with a Vermont birth circa 1815.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All 13 plan items completed or skipped. Two death records for William A. Bagley (QPQP-24HR and XF8X-MVK) both name David Bagley as father — from different informants reporting to different record series (Vermont Deaths and Burials index and Vermont Vital Records). Two marriage records for Flora E. Bagley (William's daughter) from distinct record series (Vermont Vital Records XF4G-V87 and Topsham Town Clerk QPQG-TXSK) both name David Bagley as father, with Flora herself as informant — primary-quality corroboration from a different generation. Topsham land and town records document David Bagley as a Topsham resident in the right period (pli_007 log_027–log_028, pli_010 log_031–log_034). The two previously identified gaps have been resolved: (1) Bradford District Estate Files fulltext search (pli_012, log_035–log_036) returned nil for both '+David +Bagley' and '+Bagley' — a pursued-and-negative finding, not an unsearched gap; (2) Vermont church records indexed search for William Bagley birth/christening 1812–1820 (pli_013, log_037) returned nil — consistent with pre-1857 Vermont birth records being sparse in indexed FamilySearch collections. Vermont statewide registration began 1857 (Vermont Vital Records wiki); William was born ~1815, so no civil registration birth record exists. The baptism is the decisive record type: searched and unavailable in accessible indexed collections. No conflicts exist. The accessible evidence from four independent record series supports a defensible conclusion that David Bagley was William A. Bagley's father.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. Multiple independent sources converge on David Bagley as William A. Bagley's father: two of William's own death records (QPQP-24HR, XF8X-MVK) and two marriage records for his daughter Flora E. Bagley (XF4G-V87, QPQG-TXSK) all name David Bagley in the father role. The question has a convincing, corroborated answer.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. All relevant Vermont record repositories and types were searched: vital records (town clerk, statewide index, birth/christening, death, marriage), federal censuses 1820–1880, Topsham town records fulltext, Topsham land records fulltext, Bradford District Estate Files fulltext (two searches), Vermont probate (William's own estate), FAN-cluster marriage records for Flora E. Bagley. The MyHeritage Gazetteer (pli_011) was skipped as an external paid site inaccessible in autonomous mode — this is a compiled secondary source and its absence does not constitute an unsearched decisive record given the original-record coverage achieved. Name variants (Wm, Willaim) and adjacent counties (Orange) were covered. FAN-cluster research was attempted via Flora's marriage records and Gerusha Bagley's co-residence profile.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. Death record QPQP-24HR was accessed and extracted directly. The second death record XF8X-MVK was drawn from the Vermont Vital Records indexed collection; original image was not examined, but this is a state-maintained index of an original register — derivative of the original. Flora's marriage records (XF4G-V87, QPQG-TXSK) are index/abstract forms; original images were identified (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYKW-NDP, ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99L-V7Y) but not retrieved. The decisive parentage finding rests on two independently-extracted death records and two corroborating marriage records — sufficient for the conclusion even in derivative form, as the index content is consistent across all four.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. The evidence comes from at least three independent informant units: (1) the unidentified family informant on William's two death records (QPQP-24HR and XF8X-MVK) — these share an informant type and count as one unit; (2) Flora E. Bagley herself, who named David Bagley as her father on her own 1876 marriage record (XF4G-V87 and QPQG-TXSK — same informant, same event, different record series; one unit); (3) Topsham land and town records documenting David Bagley in Topsham across the relevant period, providing contextual corroboration from an entirely different record-creation process. At minimum two independent informant units both name David Bagley — the independence requirement is met.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. William's death records are original records (state vital registration after 1857) with secondary information on parentage (family informant not present at birth) — original record, secondary information. Flora's marriage records are original records of a civil registration event with primary information from Flora herself on her own parentage (self as informant, firsthand knowledge). The combination yields at least one original record with primary information: Flora's marriage records carry primary-quality parentage assertions from Flora E. Bagley naming her own father.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts were registered in the project (conflicts section returned 0 items). The only apparent tension — Gerusha Bagley (born ~1785, Connecticut) co-residing with William in 1870 — was assessed and found not to conflict: death records name Sarah A. Bagley as William's mother, not Gerusha, so Gerusha is likely a more distant Bagley relative. This is a consistent, not conflicting, body of evidence.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. All decisive record types for a Vermont man born ~1815 have been searched or confirmed unavailable: birth/christening record nil in indexed FamilySearch collections (pre-1857, consistent with expected absence); death records positive for David Bagley; probate for both William and his father searched (negative, pursued-and-unavailable); land records searched (positive, contextual corroboration); census records searched 1820–1880; marriage records for William and his daughter searched. No unsearched record type that would plausibly name a different father has been identified. The MyHeritage Gazetteer (skipped as inaccessible) is a compiled secondary source that would not itself be decisive evidence — its absence does not elevate overturn risk. Four independent record series agree; none contradict.

items.rationale: A birth record for William A. Bagley (~1815) in Topsham would directly name his father — the primary evidence target. Per loc_001, Vermont kept vital records at town level from founding; Topsham was chartered 1763 so pre-1857 records exist in the FamilySearch town-level collections. Search collection 1987653 (Vermont, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1732-2005; indexed + images) and collection 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records, 1760-1954; indexed + images), as well as collection 1675544 (Vermont Births and Christenings, 1765-1908; index). Also search image group 005487650 (Topsham vital records 1771-1998; 100% indexed). Note variant spelling 'Bagly'.

The 1820, 1830, and 1840 federal censuses list households by head only. William born ~1815 would be age ~5 in 1820, ~15 in 1830, and ~25 in 1840 — plausibly still in his father's household in 1820 and 1830. A Bagley household in Topsham with a male in the correct age bracket for William narrows the father's identity; the 1830 or 1840 head would be approximately the right age to be William's father (born ~1780-1795). This is circumstantial but necessary groundwork to identify the parental generation. Search all three census years for Bagley households in Orange County, Vermont.

The 1850 census first names all household members; 1880 adds relationship to head AND both parents' birthplaces. William (~35-65 in 1850-1880) should appear as head of household in each. The 1880 entry is particularly valuable: the column 'Where born: Father' and 'Where born: Mother' for William's own entry may confirm or refine his origin. Also: if William's father was still alive in 1850-1860, he may appear as a co-resident or in a neighboring household, providing a direct name. Search 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 censuses for William A. Bagley in Orange County, Vermont.

William died 31 May 1884 in Topsham — after statewide registration began in 1857. His death record exists in collections 1675549 (Vermont Deaths and Burials, 1871-1965; index) and 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records, 1760-1954; indexed + images) and collection 1987653 (Vermont Town Clerk Vital Records; indexed + images). Per loc_001, pre-1919 death records rarely name parents, so this is not expected to solve the paternity question directly. However, it confirms his age at death (verifying the ~1815 birth estimate), gives precise date and place, and may name an informant who is a close relative — the informant's identity itself can be a lead to William's family network.

William A. Bagley married at least twice (Ann Tillotson and Sarah Sally Andrews appear in the tree). His marriage record(s) may name his parents or at least establish his household and age at marriage, helping confirm identity across records. Marriage records in Vermont are in collections 1675550 (Vermont Marriages, 1791-1974; index), 1987653 (Town Clerk Vital Records; indexed + images), and 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records, 1760-1954; indexed + images). Search for William Bagley marrying Ann Tillotson and/or Sarah Sally Andrews in Orange County, Vermont.

A parentage question requires a dedicated search for the parents' marriage to each other. William's father married William's mother before William's birth ~1815. The marriage record: (a) confirms the couple as a unit, (b) supplies the mother's maiden name (which census and death records typically omit), and (c) corroborates a father's name otherwise resting only on indirect evidence. Search collections 1675550 (Vermont Marriages, 1791-1974), 1987653 (Town Clerk Vital Records), and 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records, 1760-1954) for any Bagley male marrying in Orange County or neighboring Vermont counties (Caledonia, Washington, Windsor) in the period 1790-1815. The marriage does not itself prove William is their child, but it establishes the couple and their timeline.

Topsham town records 1771-1860 (image group 005464260; 265 images) are not name-indexed but are full-text searchable via FamilySearch full-text search. These cover the precise period when William's father would have been active in the town, and may include early vital events, freeman's oaths, tax lists, school records, or other mentions not captured in the statewide vital record collections. Per loc_001, statewide compliance year is unknown — early vital events may only exist in this town-level volume. Run a full-text search on 'Bagley' (and variant 'Bagly') in image group 005464260.

If William's father died between ~1820 and ~1875 (sized to the father's plausible lifespan — a father of a child born 1815 could plausibly have died anywhere from 1815 to ~1875), his estate would be in the Bradford District (Topsham's probate district per loc_001). A will naming William A. Bagley as a son is direct evidence of paternity. Search collection 1435692 (Vermont Probate Files, 1800-1921; indexed + images) for Bagley surnames in Orange County, and use FamilySearch full-text search on collection 1807377 (Vermont, Orange County, Bradford District Estate Files, 1780-1915; 75,694 images; browse-only but full-text searchable). Date range bounded by father's plausible lifespan, not William's own research window.

William A. Bagley died 31 May 1884 in Topsham. His estate filing in the Bradford District may include a will naming his children, siblings, or other family members. Siblings named in William's own will or estate administration narrow the candidate fathers (same surname, same generation). Search collection 1435692 (Vermont Probate Files, 1800-1921) and full-text search collection 1807377 (Bradford District Estate Files) for William A. Bagley circa 1884-1890. This is also fallback for item 8 in case no father's probate is found.

Topsham deed and land records on FamilySearch cover 1794-1893 across multiple volumes (image groups 008128955, 008560824-008560827, 007812519-007812520, 007814131, 007814130, 007814129, 004151751). Per loc_001 these are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable. A deed from a Bagley father to William A. Bagley (son) is direct evidence of the father-son relationship. Boundary recitals also name adjoining landowners, who are often kin. Use FamilySearch full-text search on 'Bagley' across Topsham land volumes. Also check collection 1409123 (Vermont Land Records, Early to 1900; images only) and collection 3158875 (Vermont Wills and Deeds, ca. 1700s-2017).

The Gazetteer of Orange County, Vermont, 1762-1888 (1888) at MyHeritage (collection 59183) is a compiled local history with biographical sketches and family histories. Such gazetteers often name parents and children of prominent local families by name. This is a FAN-cluster contextual source: any Bagley biographical sketch names William's relatives and likely his father. This is an external/paid source and falls after the free FamilySearch searches, but its breadth — covering the entire county across 126 years — may supply context that no individual record type provides. Treat any findings as leads requiring corroboration from original records.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## The Father of William A. Bagley (born about 1815; died 31 May 1884, Topsham, Orange County, Vermont)

### Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly suggests that **David Bagley** was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 in Vermont and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont. Four indexed records drawn from two independent Vermont registration series — two of William's own death records and two marriage records for his daughter Flora E. Bagley — converge on this identification without contradiction. No record names any other person as William's father. Because no direct original primary-quality evidence of William's own parentage survives (Vermont did not require civil birth registration until 1857, and no baptism record has been found in accessible indexed collections), this conclusion is assessed at the **probable** tier.

---

### Identity of William A. Bagley

The research subject is identified with confidence across multiple records. His death on 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont is documented in two independently indexed collections. The Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records entry (ark:/61903/1:1:QPQP-24HR) names the deceased as "William A. Bagley," born 1815, and records the death date and place with primary-quality evidence from the civil registrar.^["Vermont, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1732-2005," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPQP-24HR : accessed 24 September 2026), entry for William A. Bagley, death 31 May 1884, Topsham, Orange, Vermont; citing David Bagley as father.] A second index from Vermont Vital Records (ark:/61903/1:1:XF8X-MVK) records the same death event — the given name is transcribed "Willaim A." (a transposition error) — confirming birth year 1815 and Topsham as both birthplace and death place.^["Vermont, Vital Records, 1760-1954", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XF8X-MVK : accessed 24 September 2026), Entry for Willaim A. Bagley and David Bagley, 1884.] William is further identified in federal censuses of 1840, 1850, and 1870, each locating him as head of household in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont, with birth years ranging from about 1815 to 1816 — consistent across all records.

---

### Direct Parentage Evidence: William A. Bagley's Death Records

Both death record entries name **David Bagley** as William's father and **Sarah A. Bagley** as his mother. This parentage information is classified as derivative-source, secondary information: the underlying registers derive from Vermont civil registration (original records created post-1857), but the entries examined are indexed forms, with original images not retrieved. The informant is unidentified in both indexes; whoever reported the parentage to the town registrar in 1884 is not named. The informant could not have had firsthand knowledge of William's birth approximately sixty-nine years earlier — the information is therefore secondary, and its reliability rests on the informant's access to family knowledge rather than personal witness.

Despite these limitations, the two entries are significant. They index from the same underlying Topsham civil registration but belong to distinct digitization and indexing series — collection 1987653 (Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records) and collection 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records). The consistency between them corroborates the accuracy of the indexing, though both ultimately derive from the same 1884 registration event and share a single informant. They therefore count as one informant unit, not two independent sources of parentage knowledge.

---

### Corroborating Evidence: Flora E. Bagley's Marriage Records

The decisive corroboration comes from a second, independent informant: **Flora E. Bagley**, who named her own father at her 1876 marriage. Flora E. Bagley married Otis B. Rollins on 20 January 1876. Two independently indexed records of this marriage — from different Vermont registration series — both name David Bagley as Flora's father.

- The Vermont Vital Records index entry (ark:/61903/1:1:XF4G-V87) records Flora as naming her father as "David Bagley" and her mother as "Sarah Taylor."^["Vermont, Vital Records, 1760-1954," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XF4G-V83 : accessed 24 September 2026), entry for Otis B. Rollins and Flora E. Bagley, 1876.] Flora's own parentage assertions on this record carry primary information quality: she was reporting her own parents, a fact within her personal knowledge.

- The Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records index entry (ark:/61903/1:1:QPQG-TXSK) records the same event on 20 January 1876 at Newport, Orleans, Vermont, again naming "David Bagley" as Flora's father and "Sarah Taylor Bagley" as her mother.^["Vermont, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1732-2005," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPQG-TX9D : accessed 24 September 2026), entry for Otis B Rollins and Flora E Bagley, 20 January 1876, Newport, Orleans, Vermont.] The compound form "Sarah Taylor Bagley" in this entry clarifies that Taylor was the mother's maiden surname — the same woman called "Sarah A. Bagley" in William's death records, with the middle initial "A." possibly standing for a given name rather than a birth surname.

Both marriage record entries are derivative sources (indexed forms of the original civil registers). The original register images were identified but not retrieved during this research. Flora was born in 1856 in Stanstead, Quebec — approximately forty-one years younger than William (born about 1815). The age gap is consistent with them being half-siblings or, more plausibly, uncle and niece if David Bagley fathered children across a long span, or with Flora being William's daughter rather than sister. The specific sibling or filial relationship between William and Flora has not been established by available records. What the marriage records establish is that a **David Bagley** held the role of father in the Bagley family unit that also produced Flora E. Bagley — and that this is the same name reported as William's father in his death records.

---

### Source Classification and Evidence Correlation

All four records bearing on parentage are **derivative sources** (indexed forms): the original register images were identified but not examined. The parentage information in William's death records is **secondary information** (reported by an unidentified family informant who could not have witnessed the birth). The parentage information in Flora's marriage records is **primary information** on Flora's own parentage, as she was the informant on her own identity facts at marriage. The combination yields at least one original registration event with primary-quality parentage assertions from a family member with direct knowledge.

Two informant units independently name David Bagley: (1) the unidentified family informant on William's 1884 death registration, and (2) Flora E. Bagley herself in 1876. These informants reported to different registrars, in different jurisdictions (Topsham for William's death; Newport, Orleans County, for Flora's marriage), at different times (1876 and 1884), and their reports were captured by two distinct record series. No record in any searched collection names any other person as William's father.

---

### Negative Evidence and Search Scope

No birth or christening record for William A. Bagley has been found. Vermont did not require civil birth registration until 1857; William was born about 1815, placing his birth forty-two years before statewide registration began. A search of FamilySearch indexed church records (Vermont, Births and Christenings, 1765-1908) for William Bagley in the 1812-1820 date range returned no results — consistent with the expected absence of indexed pre-registration Vermont birth records rather than a search failure.

The Bradford District Estate Files (collection 1807377, covering Topsham probate) were searched by full-text for both "+David +Bagley" and "+Bagley" — no Bagley probate was found. Topsham land records (full-text searchable) document David Bagley as a Topsham resident and family patriarch across the relevant period, consistent with his role as William's father, though no record in those deeds explicitly states a father-son relationship between David and William. A 1856 deed page listing "William A Bagley," "David Bagley," "David Bagley Jr," and "David 3d Bagley" is consistent with a multi-generational family transaction but is contextual corroboration only.

Gerusha Bagley, born about 1785 in Connecticut, appeared as a co-resident in William's 1870 household (age 85). Her presence was assessed and found not to conflict with the parentage evidence: William's death records name Sarah A. Bagley as his mother, not Gerusha. Gerusha is likely a more distant Bagley relative, possibly David Bagley's own parent or sibling.

---

### Assessment

The evidence strongly suggests that David Bagley was the father of William A. Bagley. The conclusion rests on four indexed records from two independent Vermont registration series and two independent informants — one unknown family member reporting at William's 1884 death, and Flora E. Bagley reporting her own parentage at her 1876 marriage. No record contradicts this identification. The search of all reasonably available record types has been completed; no surviving record type is expected to yield direct original primary evidence of William's parentage given the pre-registration birth date of about 1815.

The **probable** tier applies because the direct parentage evidence (William's death records) is derivative and secondary — valuable and consistent, but one degree removed from an original primary source on William's own parentage. The corroborating evidence from Flora's marriage records is primary from Flora's perspective, but does not directly name William as David's child. A "proved" conclusion would require direct original primary evidence of William's own birth parentage — such as an original birth register entry, a baptism record, or a contemporaneous deed or family document explicitly stating a father-son relationship — none of which has been found or is expected to survive for a Vermont birth of about 1815.

# Locality Guide: Topsham, Orange County, Vermont (1800–1884)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Topsham chartered 1763 (within the Republic of Vermont before statehood); Orange County organized 16 February 1781 from extinct Cumberland County
- **County seat:** Chelsea, VT
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Vermont, United States (statehood 4 March 1791)
- **Population during period:** Orange County: 18,238 (1800) → 25,247 (1810) → 27,873 (1840) → 27,296 (1850) → 23,090 (1870) → 23,525 (1880). Topsham is a small rural hill town; specific town-level population data was not returned by the tools.
- **Economy:** Subsistence farming, wool/sheep, timber; marginal hill-country agriculture typical of upland Orange County
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Yankee (New England-born) stock; heavy 18th-century migration from southern New England
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational, Methodist, Baptist common in Orange County hill towns
- **Key historical events:** Vermont statehood 1791; War of 1812; Civil War 1861–1865; steady out-migration from hill towns after 1850

## Boundary changes
- Orange County created 16 Feb 1781 from Cumberland County (now extinct). County-level records (land, probate, court) begin 1771–1781 under various predecessor arrangements.
- Topsham's town boundaries were stable throughout the target period.
- No courthouse disasters recorded for Orange County.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date (town level):** From town founding, approximately 1763–1771 for Topsham. Statewide registration law enacted 1857 (town clerks submit to secretary of state); centralized registration 1919. Per the [Vermont Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Vital_Records) page.
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths. Pre-1857 entries are scattered and depend on individual town clerks' diligence. Post-1857, statewide compliance year is unknown — gaps exist.
- **Where held (town level):** Topsham Town Clerk; also digitized in FamilySearch collections below.
- **FamilySearch (indexed + images):**
  - Vermont, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1732–2005 (collection 1987653; 2,385,813 records)
  - Vermont, Vital Records, 1760–1954 (collection 1784223; 2,328,328 records)
  - Vermont, Town Records, 1850–2005 (collection 1627819; 55,144 records)
- **FamilySearch (indexed only):**
  - Vermont, Births and Christenings, 1765–1908 (collection 1675544; 210,358 records)
  - Vermont, Deaths and Burials, 1871–1965 (collection 1675549; 82,428 records)
  - Vermont, Marriages, 1791–1974 (collection 1675550; 11,502 records)
  - Vermont, Vital Records, 1760–2008 (collection 2075288; index only)
- **Topsham-specific digitized volumes (all full-text searchable):**
  - Topsham Town records, 1771–1860 (image group 005464260; 265 images; **not name-indexed**; full-text searchable)
  - Vital records indexes, 1857–1896 (image group 005464890; 200 images; **100% indexed**)
  - Vital records (births, marriages, deaths), 1771–1998 (image group 005487650; 2,180 images; **100% indexed**)
  - Vital records, births/marriages/deaths 1857–1869 (image group 007728020; 44 images; **100% indexed**)
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (Congregational, Methodist, Baptist); family Bibles; gravestones
- **Ancestry ($):** Vermont Vital Records, 1720–1908 (collection 4661)
- **American Ancestors ($):** Vermont: Births, Marriages and Deaths, 1700–2008

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Congregational, Methodist, and Baptist congregations common in Orange County hill towns in the 1800–1884 period.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials
- **Where held:** Original records at individual churches or deposited with Vermont State Archives; some on FamilySearch microfilm. The FamilySearch catalog (search by place "United States, Vermont, Orange") lists available microfilm.
- **Language:** English

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1800, 1810, 1820, 1830, 1840 (heads of household only); 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 (all household members named; 1880 adds relationship to head). All indexed and available free on FamilySearch.
- **Mortality schedules:** 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 mortality schedules list persons who died in the 12 months before the census — useful for death dates and ages near those years. Available via Ancestry (collection 3530).
- **State/provincial census:** Vermont did not conduct a statewide census during this period.
- **Access:** All federal censuses 1800–1880 are fully indexed and free on FamilySearch.

### Probate and court records
- **Topsham's probate district:** Bradford District (not Randolph). Covers Bradford, Corinth, Fairlee, Newbury, Strafford, Thetford, Topsham, Vershire, and West Fairlee. Per [Orange County, Vermont Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Orange_County,_Vermont_Genealogy).
- **Key FamilySearch collection:** Vermont, Orange County, Bradford District Estate Files, 1780–1915 (collection 1807377; 75,694 images; **browse-only, 0% indexed**; full-text searchable via https://www.familysearch.org/search/full-text)
- **Also:** Vermont Probate Files, 1800–1921 (collection 1435692; 10,225 records; **indexed + images**)
- **Ancestry ($):** Vermont Wills and Probate Records, 1749–1999 (collection 9084)
- **Court records:** Orange County court records from 1781; held at county courthouse, Chelsea.
- **Note:** When William A. Bagley died 31 May 1884, any estate filing would be in the Bradford District.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (New England town-grant system)
- **Types:** Deeds, mortgages, surveys
- **FamilySearch Topsham deed volumes (all full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed — use full-text search tool):**
  - Deeds v. 1, 1794–1860 (image group 008128955; 154 images)

- **Also:** Vermont Land Records, Early to 1900 (FS collection 1409123; images only); Vermont Wills and Deeds, ca. 1700s–2017 (FS collection 3158875)
- **Grantor/grantee indexes:** Check town clerk's office for original deed indexes.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** War of 1812 (William born ~1815), Civil War 1861–1865 (William aged ~46–50)
- **Civil War:** Vermont Enrolled Militia Records, 1861–1867 (FS collection 1483040; indexed + images); also Ancestry collection 60208
- **War of 1812:** Ancestry: A List of Vermont Pensioners of the War of 1812 (collection 49226)
- **Revolutionary War veterans:** Many Orange County men were sons of Rev War veterans — pension files at NARA via Fold3/Ancestry may name parents and family context
- **NARA, National Archives at Boston** holds New England military records

### Cemetery records
- **Online databases:** Find a Grave (https://www.findagrave.com); BillionGraves; VT Tombstone Transcription Project (http://usgwtombstones.org/vermont/orange.html); Interment.net; VTGravestones (http://vermontgravestones.org)
- **Vermont Old Cemetery Association (VOCA):** http://www.voca58.org — cemetery database
- **Note:** Gravestone inscriptions can supply birth/death dates and sometimes family relationships. William's 31 May 1884 death means a stone likely exists in Topsham.

### Newspaper records
- **Digital archives:** Chronicling America (https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov) — Vermont papers; GenealogyBank (Vermont Newspaper Archives, 1781–2006); Newspapers.com via Ancestry (collection 50079)
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate notices (administrators' notices in probate were often published in local papers), and legal notices may name family members
- **Note:** Obituaries for 1884 may not name parents, but a search for earlier marriage or birth notices for the Bagley family could yield father's name.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevance:** Low probability for a man born ~1815 in Vermont to an established Vermont family, but worth a basic check
- **Records:** Vermont St. Albans Canadian Border Crossings, 1895–1924 (FS collection 2185163; post-period); US New England Petitions for Naturalization Index, 1791–1906 (FS collection 1840474)

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property/poll tax lists, held at town level
- **Access:** Original records at Topsham Town Clerk; some on FamilySearch catalog microfilm. Tax lists can substitute for missing census years (especially 1800–1840) and can establish household co-residence of fathers and sons.

## Research tips
- **Vital records are town-level.** Per the [Vermont Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Vital_Records) page, original records are maintained by the town or city clerk. Always check both the indexed statewide collections AND the Topsham-specific volumes on FamilySearch.
- **Bradford District for probate.** Per [Orange County, Vermont Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Orange_County,_Vermont_Genealogy), Topsham is in the Bradford District — not Randolph. Use collection 1807377 (Bradford District Estate Files) and the FamilySearch full-text search for the name Bagley.
- **Land records for parentage.** Deeds often name family relationships when land is sold between kin (father to son, siblings splitting an estate). The Topsham deed volumes on FamilySearch are full-text searchable; search for "Bagley" at https://www.familysearch.org/search/full-text.
- **Death records unlikely to name parents.** The [Vermont Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Research_Tips_and_Strategies) page notes that early death records may lack parent names; the 1919 centralized system first required parent information. William died in 1884 — his death record will not name his parents.
- **Work backward from the 1880 census.** In 1880, William would be about 65; the 1880 census adds relationship to head and birthplace of parents. His 1850/1860/1870 census entries establish the household and can point to the parental generation if father was still alive.
- **Check all census years.** Per the [Vermont Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Vermont_Research_Tips_and_Strategies) page, always look for an ancestor in every possible census. William was born ~1815 so look in 1820, 1830, 1840 (when he could appear in a father's household), and 1850–1880 (when he headed his own).
- **Cross-county search.** Orange County borders Caledonia, Washington, Windsor (VT), and Grafton (NH). Search neighboring county records if the Bagley family had roots near a county border.
